title: What is a deductible?

scenes.text: Your insurance *won't* pay the first part of your bill?
scenes.voice: Did you know your insurance might not pay the first part of your hospital bill?

scenes.text: That first part is called a *deductible*.
scenes.voice: That first part has a name. It's called a deductible.

scenes.text: It's the amount *you* pay before insurance starts paying.
scenes.sub: Some plans call it an excess.
scenes.voice: A deductible is the amount you pay yourself, before your insurance starts covering the rest. Some plans call it an excess.

scenes.sub: You pay RM1,000. The plan covers the rest, up to its limits.
scenes.voice: Say your bill is five thousand ringgit, and your deductible is one thousand. You pay the first thousand, and the plan covers the rest, up to its limits.

scenes.text: Higher deductible = *lower* premium. Lower deductible = *higher* premium.
scenes.voice: Here's the trade off. A higher deductible usually means a lower premium. A lower deductible usually means you pay more each month.

scenes.text: Pick one you could *actually pay* in an emergency.
scenes.voice: So choose a deductible you could actually afford to pay if something happened tomorrow.

scenes.text: Follow for one *insurance concept* at a time.
scenes.voice: Follow for more insurance concepts, explained simply.

caption:
What's a deductible, and why does it change your premium? 🧾

A deductible is the amount you pay first, before your insurance covers the rest. Higher deductible → usually lower premium. Lower deductible → usually higher premium.

The right one is an amount you could actually pay in an emergency.
